summary.headline: Mach Travel Solutions Q2 FY27 revenue rose 174.7% YoY to INR204.53 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.0% from 12.81%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR204.53 crore, up 174.7% YoY and 41.7% QoQ, with H1 revenue at INR348.86 crore. PAT rose 47% YoY to INR9.26 crore, but PAT margin compressed to 4.50% from 8.35%, as management prioritised customer acquisition across new verticals and built out headcount to about 350. Management revised FY27 revenue guidance to more than 2.5x FY26 revenue, while the B2C platform remains in public beta. Sequential margin improved modestly in Q2 versus Q1.

segments.name: MICE
segments.commentary: Management puts MICE at about 60% to 65% of total business and says it remains the core and biggest revenue generator. The team was not disturbed during the transition.

segments.name: Government and institutional
segments.commentary: Management cited 15% to 20% of revenue, with an empanelment with the Madhya Pradesh government for up to about 10,000 pilgrims under Mukhyamantri Tirth Yatra. Empanelments also cited in Karnataka and IRCTC; applications pending in Bihar and UP.

segments.name: Corporate travel
segments.commentary: Launched in April 2026, now about 10% to 15% of business, with more than 140 corporate clients as of 30 September, up from more than 100 in Q1 and zero on 31 March.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Balance-sheet revenue is only commissions, about 3% to 4% of the mix, despite high volumes.

segments.name: Leisure (incl. visa)
segments.commentary: About 5% to 7% of business. Includes visa services and leisure travel.

segments.name: Inbound
segments.commentary: Early stage: 3 inbound groups secured from France, Belgium and the USA, totalling 71 international travellers. No revenue trajectory given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target raised to more than 2.5x FY26 revenue, which management says is supported by pipeline and a strong order book.
Management guided to about 25% YoY growth over the medium term, describing FY27 as an exceptional growth year.
Management expects PAT margin to improve gradually as new customers are added and the cost base stays flat; no PAT target was committed, though it said pro-rata PAT could double.
No fundraising planned for now; management said it may raise funds after listing on the Main Board, about 9 to 10 months away.
Next investor call guided for late January or first week of February 2027.
capex_capacity: Noida office is 13,000 sq ft and can seat 250 to 275 employees; only about 110 currently sit there.
Company operates 7 offices (Noida, New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Bhubaneswar, Ahmedabad), each said to fit about 90 people.
Headcount grew from about 70 to about 350 team members; management said cost base would stay similar as business ramps.
Empanelments are done twice a year, in early April and October, which management said determines when new business is added.
B2C platform machtravel.com and mobile app opened for public beta on 31 August 2026; full commercial launch timing not given.
demand_pricing: Corporate clients rose to more than 140 across automotive, engineering, pharma, BFSI, technology, healthcare, education, FMCG, infrastructure and manufacturing.

Government and institutional: Madhya Pradesh Tirth Yatra order for up to about 10,000 pax; in talks with Bihar and UP; management said payments are flowing with some delays, and a group going to NASA (USA) has 80% advance.
Government and institutional margins are said to be higher than peers due to volume buying power; management said little cross-selling is possible in this segment.
Management said one long-standing MICE client of about 8 to 9 years has signed a corporate ticketing contract with a SBT tool limit.
Management said the Q2 margin decline reflects aggressive customer acquisition and it is compromising margin to win business.

qa_highlights.question: How will inbound travel scale, and what is the timeline for it to become meaningful?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a timeline is hard to give at this stage. A small inbound team is in place, and growth in numbers is expected within 6 months; fairs such as WTM London and Dubai are planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise, and will expansion need more debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher turnover raised funding needs and it paid INR1.8 crore of interest in H1. It is not raising funds now and may do so after Main Board listing.

qa_highlights.question: Why has PAT fallen versus last year's levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company was revamped about 6 months ago and is being aggressive in acquiring business, so it has compromised PAT margin. Management expects margins to improve gradually and sees Q2 margin up marginally from Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin decline justified given the headcount ramp from 70 to 300+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the team was ramped up to about 350 to add new business, and that H1 PAT already equals FY26's PAT. It said cost would stay flat while new customers are added, so profitability would rise. No PAT target was committed.

qa_highlights.question: How is cross-selling progressing and how is success measured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said each corporate client opens access to employees' leisure travel and MICE needs. It gave one example of an 8 to 9 year MICE client now on SBT. No cross-sell metrics were disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What are the collection cycles in government and institutional business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payments on the Punjab Yatra are coming with some delays and it is focused on recovery. It said it is comfortable with the cycle, pointing to the programme running since April.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin at 7.0% versus 12.81% a year ago, and PAT margin at 4.50% versus 8.35%, with management prioritising acquisition over profitability.
Working capital intensity: revenue growth is requiring more working capital, and finance cost rose to INR1.2 crore in Q2 from INR0.21 crore.
Collection delays in government and institutional business, including the Punjab Yatra, which management called manageable.
Inbound and B2C platform revenue contribution remains unquantified, and the commercial launch date is not set.
Management did not disclose a breakdown of revenue by segment in INR terms, and gave only approximate percentages.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, with the 2.5x FY27 revenue target and 25% medium-term growth stated repeatedly. Noticeably defensive on profitability: management acknowledged the margin compression, attributed it to deliberate customer acquisition, and gave no PAT target. Evasive on inbound timelines, B2C launch dates and segment-level financials.
key_quotes: And we have compromised on our PAT margins.
